title: Tesla, the electric car maker, goes public
what: Tesla Motors sold 13.3 million shares at 17 dollars on the Nasdaq on 29 June, raising 226 million dollars; it is the first American car maker to go public since Ford in 1956. Tesla builds the Roadster, an expensive electric sports car, and plans a family saloon, the Model S. It loses money; in May it bought the former NUMMI car plant in Fremont, California, from Toyota, which is buying 50 million dollars of Tesla shares.
why: The listing beat. From here the share rose more than 200-fold by 2026, with near-death moments in 2013, 2018 and 2019 along the way.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (IPO, NUMMI, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (Toyota partnership, read 2026-10-03)

title: Panasonic and Toyota deals send Tesla soaring
what: Panasonic, the world's leading maker of lithium-ion battery cells, bought 30 million dollars of Tesla shares at 21.15 dollars. Tesla's third-quarter revenue rose 10% to 31.2 million dollars and its loss narrowed to 34.9 million. At the Los Angeles motor show Toyota showed an electric RAV4 'powered by Tesla'. The shares closed at a record 35.47 dollars on 24 November, more than double the IPO price.
why: +62% in a month on partnerships rather than profits; analysts already warned it was overdone, and the share gave back a quarter in December.
source: Tesla 8-K exhibits of 4 November 2010 (Panasonic) and 9 November 2010 (Q3 results), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312510248220/dex991.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312510254219/dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); The Mercury News, 'Tesla Motors stock shows strong gains since IPO', 26 November 2010, https://www.mercurynews.com/2010/11/26/tesla-motors-stock-shows-strong-gains-since-ipo/ (read 2026-10-03)

title: The Model S goes into production
what: Tesla began building and delivering the Model S, its electric luxury saloon, at the Fremont factory in June. Production of the Roadster sports car ended in January. The company is still losing money and must now build cars in volume.
why: The car that made Tesla; it later won Motor Trend's Car of the Year. The production ramp nearly broke the company in early 2013.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla says it will make its first profit
what: On 31 March Tesla announced that it delivered more than 4,750 Model S cars in the first quarter, beating its target of 4,500, and that it now expects to be profitable for the quarter for the first time. 'Profitability is what makes a company real. Tesla is here to stay,' said Elon Musk.
why: +42%. In hindsight, Tesla had been running out of money early in 2013, and Musk had discussed a sale to Google.
source: Tesla 8-K exhibit of 1 April 2013, 'Tesla Model S sales exceed target; profitability guidance amended upward', https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312513135229/d514482dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: First profit and the government loan repaid
what: Tesla reported its first quarterly profit in its ten-year history on 8 May: 11 million dollars on record revenue of 562 million, with 4,900 cars delivered. It then raised 1 billion dollars from new shares and convertible bonds, and on 22 May repaid its 465 million dollar government loan nine years early, the first carmaker in the programme to do so.
why: +81%, Tesla's best month in the game: the moment the 'Tesla story' began.
source: Tesla First Quarter 2013 Shareholder Letter, 8 May 2013, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312513207910/d532640dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); The Denver Post, 'Tesla Motors fully repays $465 million federal loan nine years early', 22 May 2013, https://www.denverpost.com/2013/05/22/tesla-motors-fully-repays-465-million-federal-loan-nine-years-early/ (read 2026-10-03)

title: Model S fires hit the shares
what: A third Model S caught fire after hitting road debris at high speed, and Tesla's shares fell more than 20% in November. In each case the car had warned the occupants to stop. Tesla is extending its warranty to cover fire damage.
why: The first big setback after the 2013 rally; Tesla added a titanium shield under the battery, and regulators closed their inquiry in March 2014.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Record deliveries and a plan for a giant battery factory
what: Tesla delivered a record 6,892 Model S in the fourth quarter, had positive free cash flow and expects deliveries to grow by more than 55% in 2014. On 26 February it announced 1.6 billion dollars of convertible bonds to help pay for a huge battery factory, the 'Gigafactory', to make cheaper batteries for a mass-market car.
why: +35% as investors bought the vision of a mass-market electric car; the Gigafactory in Nevada was built with Panasonic.
source: Tesla Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2013 Shareholder Letter, 19 February 2014, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312514058778/d676319dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); Tesla 8-K exhibit of 26 February 2014 (convertible notes), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312514069704/d685452dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (bonds for the Gigafactory, read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla starts delivering the Model X
what: Tesla began shipping its third car, the Model X sport utility vehicle with rear doors that open upwards like wings, in September. It had 25,000 pre-orders. Deliveries were first planned for early 2014.
why: The Model X broadened the range but trouble with the falcon-wing doors had delayed it; the next big step was the cheaper Model 3.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_X (read 2026-10-03)

title: 325,000 people reserve the Model 3
what: Tesla has unveiled the Model 3, its first car for the mass market, cheaper than its earlier models. Within a week more than 325,000 people paid to reserve one.
why: The reservation queue proved the demand; building the car turned into 'production hell' in 2018.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_3 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla buys SolarCity
what: Tesla completed its purchase of the solar installer SolarCity in an all-stock deal worth about 2.6 billion dollars, merging it with its battery storage business into Tesla Energy. The deal is controversial among Tesla shareholders.
why: Controversial: SolarCity's liquidity problems had not been disclosed to Tesla's shareholders; a Delaware court cleared Musk in 2022.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SolarCity (read 2026-10-03)

title: The first Model 3s are delivered
what: Tesla delivered the first Model 3s to customers in July. The cheaper car is meant to turn Tesla from a niche luxury maker into a mass producer. Tesla Motors renamed itself Tesla, Inc. in February.
why: Profile change in the game. The ramp-up went badly and brought Tesla close to running out of money in 2018.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Model_3 (read 2026-10-03)

title: Production hell, a fatal crash and a big recall
what: Tesla is far behind its targets for Model 3 production, and heavy spending on automated factories is draining its cash; it is one of the most shorted shares on the market. In March a Model X driver was killed in a crash while using Autopilot, and on 29 March Tesla recalled 123,000 older Model S cars over corroding power-steering bolts.
why: -22%: the low point of 'production hell', which put Tesla under severe financial pressure.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (production hell, March 2018 crash, recall of 29 March 2018, read 2026-10-03)

title: 'Funding secured': Musk tweets about taking Tesla private
what: On 7 August Elon Musk wrote on Twitter that he was considering taking Tesla private at 420 dollars a share and that 'funding' was 'secured'. The shares jumped, then fell back as doubts grew about whether the money was really lined up.
why: One of the most consequential tweets by a chief executive; it led to SEC fraud charges and many lawsuits. Review 2026-10: removed the outcome (money not lined up, plan came to nothing), established only later.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Musk settles with the SEC and loses the chairmanship
what: Musk settled securities-fraud charges brought by the SEC over his 'funding secured' statements: he pays a 20 million dollar fine, gives up the chairmanship of Tesla, and his tweets will be reviewed by Tesla's lawyers; two independent directors join the board.
why: Musk stayed chief executive; Q3 then brought a surprise profit. Review 2026-10: cut the FBI sentence: not in the source and possibly reported only in October.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: A surprise profit: 'a truly historic quarter'
what: Tesla reported a third-quarter profit of 312 million dollars and free cash flow of 881 million on 24 October, with a gross margin above 20% on the Model 3. It expects to stay profitable in the fourth quarter.
why: +27%: the Model 3 ramp finally worked, for a while.
source: Tesla Third Quarter 2018 Update, 24 October 2018, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000156459018024902/tsla-ex991_6.htm (read 2026-10-03)

title: Shanghai and profits send Tesla soaring
what: Tesla said on 29 January that 2019 was a turning point: it returned to profit in the second half and generated 1.1 billion dollars of free cash flow. Its Shanghai factory, its first outside the US, started building the Model 3 less than ten months after construction began, and production of the Model Y has started in Fremont. The shares rose more than 50% in January.
why: +56%: the start of the great rally of 2020 (+1,004% from August 2019 to August 2020), driven by profits and Chinese production.
source: Tesla Q4 and FY2019 Update, 29 January 2020, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000156459020002489/tsla-ex991_340.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (Gigafactory Shanghai, read 2026-10-03)

title: Profitable even in a pandemic quarter
what: On 29 April Tesla reported a profit for the first quarter, the first time it has been profitable in the seasonally weak first quarter, despite factory closures. It was its third profitable quarter in a row.
why: +49%: a profit despite the factory closures.
source: Tesla Q1 2020 Update, 29 April 2020, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000156459020019776/tsla-ex9901_96.htm (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla becomes the world's most valuable car maker
what: In July Tesla became the world's most valuable car maker by stock-market value, although it builds far fewer cars than the big established makers. It also reported a fourth straight quarterly profit, which meets a condition for joining the S&P 500 index.
why: +33%; index inclusion became the next catalyst.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. ('Starting in July 2020, it has been the world's most valuable automaker', read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Tesla stock jumps on carmaker's addition to the S&P 500', 16 November 2020, https://www.cnbc.com/2020/11/16/tesla-stock-jumps-on-news-company-is-joining-sp-500.html (profit record, read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla splits its shares five for one
what: On 11 August Tesla announced a five-for-one stock split, to make the shares more accessible to employees and investors; shareholders on record on 21 August receive four extra shares for each one. The shares rose 74% in August.
why: A split changes nothing about the value of the company, but it set off Tesla's second-best month. (The game's prices are adjusted for the split.)
source: Tesla 8-K exhibit 'Tesla Announces a Five-for-One Stock Split', 11 August 2020, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000156459020039353/tsla-ex991_6.htm (read 2026-10-03); data/out/tsla.json (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla will join the S&P 500
what: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced on 16 November that Tesla will join the S&P 500 index on 21 December, after five consecutive quarterly profits. Index funds will have to buy the shares; Tesla will be one of the ten most valuable companies in the index. The shares jumped more than 13% in after-hours trading.
why: +46%: the index buying lifted the share again in December; Tesla entered as the most valuable company ever added.
source: CNBC, 'Tesla stock jumps on carmaker's addition to the S&P 500', 16 November 2020, https://www.cnbc.com/2020/11/16/tesla-stock-jumps-on-news-company-is-joining-sp-500.html (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla buys 1.5 billion dollars of bitcoin
what: Tesla's annual report revealed that it had invested about 1.5 billion dollars in the cryptocurrency bitcoin, and it said it would soon accept bitcoin as payment for cars. Critics say this clashes with Tesla's environmental mission.
why: A sign of the speculative mood around Tesla in early 2021; Tesla stopped accepting bitcoin after 49 days.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Hertz orders 100,000 Teslas and Tesla is worth a trillion
what: On 25 October the rental company Hertz said it will buy 100,000 Model 3s for its fleet, and Tesla's market value passed 1 trillion dollars for the first time, making it the sixth American company to reach that mark.
why: +44%: the peak of the Tesla bubble came the next month, in November 2021.
source: NPR, 'Tesla's market value hits $1 trillion after Hertz agrees to buy 100,000 of its cars', 25 October 2021, https://www.npr.org/2021/10/25/1048953565/hertz-will-buy-100-000-teslas-electric-vehicles (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Musk bids for Twitter and sells Tesla shares
what: On 14 April Elon Musk offered to buy Twitter for about 43 billion dollars, and on 25 April Twitter accepted. Within three days of the agreement Musk sold 8.5 billion dollars of his Tesla shares to help pay for it.
why: -19%: Twitter became the overhang on Tesla for the rest of 2022.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acquisition_of_Twitter_by_Elon_Musk (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla's worst month as Musk is busy with Twitter
what: Tesla shares fell to their lowest in more than two years in late December and have lost more than half their value since the start of October. Investors worry that Twitter, which Musk bought in October and now runs, takes too much of his time.
why: -37%, the worst month in the game; the worst stretch ran from November 2021 to December 2022 (-68%).
source: The Guardian, 'Tesla stock marks lowest close in years as investors worry about Musk's focus', 27 December 2022, https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2022/dec/27/tesla-stock-drops-lowest-close-years-elon-musk (read 2026-10-03); WSJ, 'Tesla Shares Head for Worst Year Ever as Elon Musk Focuses on Twitter', 24 December 2022 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Price cuts and a profit beat spark a rebound
what: Tesla cut the prices of its cars in the United States in January to revive demand. Its fourth-quarter results on 25 January beat profit forecasts, although margins are shrinking and the price cuts will squeeze them further.
why: +41% from the December low; the price cuts started a price war among electric car makers.
source: Aswath Damodaran, 'Tesla in 2023: A Return to Reality, The Beginning of the End or Time to Buy', 26 January 2023, https://aswathdamodaran.substack.com/p/tesla-in-2023-a-return-to-reality (read 2026-10-03); Tesla Q4 and FY 2022 Update, 25 January 2023, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000156459023000799/tsla-ex991_127.htm (read 2026-10-03)

title: The Cybertruck finally arrives
what: Tesla delivered the first Cybertrucks, its stainless-steel pickup announced four years ago, on 30 November, after several delays.
why: A symbol of Musk's ambitions, delivered late.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Cybertruck (read 2026-10-03)

title: Tesla warns growth will slow
what: Tesla said on 24 January that its vehicle volume growth in 2024 'may be notably lower' than in 2023, as it is 'between two major growth waves' and works on a cheaper next-generation car.
why: -25%: the end of the growth story for cars; from 2024 the bull case moved to robotaxis and robots.
source: Tesla Q4 and FY 2023 Update, 24 January 2024, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000095017024007073/tsla-ex99_1.htm (read 2026-10-03); WSJ, 'Tesla Projects Slower Growth in 2024 as EV Demand Softens', 24 January 2024 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Musk's politics hit Tesla's sales and shares
what: In February, Musk's first full month leading the Department of Government Efficiency, which is cutting the federal workforce, Tesla shares fell 28%, their worst month since December 2022. Protesters gathered at Tesla showrooms, Tesla's sales in the EU and UK nearly halved in January, and its German sales fell 76% in February. Fourth-quarter car revenue had fallen 8%.
why: The brand damage of Musk's politics; the shares recovered when he stepped back from government in May.
source: CNBC, 'Tesla's worst month since 2022 coincided with Elon Musk's first full month in White House', 4 March 2025, https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/04/elon-musk-first-month-in-white-house-was-tesla-worst-month-since-2022.html (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (protests, European sales, read 2026-10-03)

title: A feud with Trump, then the first robotaxis
what: On 5 June a public row broke out between Musk and President Trump, who suggested cutting government contracts with Musk's companies; Tesla lost about 150 billion dollars of market value in a day. Later in the month Tesla began a small robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, with safety supervisors on board.
why: Musk's political and self-driving bets in one month; the robotaxi became the core of the bull case.
source: Reuters, 'Trump-Musk row slams Tesla shares, $150 billion in market value wiped out', 5 June 2025; BBC, 'Tesla shares tumble as Trump-Musk feud erupts', 5 June 2025, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cy902rv7q8do (read 2026-10-03); Finbold, '$1,000 invested in Tesla stock when Robotaxi launched a year ago is now worth', 23 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Elon Musk says Tesla taking safety supervisors out of some Robotaxi vehicles in Austin', 22 January 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Musk buys a billion dollars of Tesla shares
what: Elon Musk bought about 1 billion dollars of Tesla shares, adding to his roughly 13% stake, in what investors took as a vote of confidence; the shares jumped more than 6% on 15 September. Musk wants more control of Tesla as he pushes it into robotaxis, automation and artificial intelligence.
why: +33%: the AI-and-robots narrative took over from the car business.
source: BBC, 'Musk buys $1bn worth of Tesla shares', 15 September 2025, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp982z3xrz7o (read 2026-10-03); CBS News, 'Tesla's stock surges after CEO Elon Musk buys $1 billion worth of shares', 15 September 2025 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: Shareholders approve a trillion-dollar pay plan for Musk
what: On 6 November Tesla shareholders approved, with more than 75% of votes, a pay package worth up to 1 trillion dollars for Musk over ten years, if he meets specific goals set by the board.
why: Locked Musk in as chief executive; the price is the bet on Optimus and robotaxis.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03); CNBC, 'Tesla says shareholders approve Musk's $1 trillion pay plan with over 75% voting in favor', 6 November 2025 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

title: BYD overtakes Tesla, and the Model S and X are dropped
what: Full-year figures published on 2 January showed that China's BYD sold more electric cars than Tesla in 2025 (2.26 million against 1.64 million), ending Tesla's run as the largest maker. On 28 January Musk said Tesla will stop making the Model S and Model X in the second quarter and use the Fremont space to build its Optimus humanoid robot.
why: Tesla officially becomes a robot-and-AI story; the car that made it, the Model S, is retired.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)

title: Record deliveries, but profits disappoint
what: Tesla delivered a record 480,126 cars in the second quarter, but on 22 July it reported earnings of 33 cents a share against expected 53 cents; its operating margin fell to 1.4%, regulatory credit income collapsed and spending on factories and AI more than doubled, so it burned cash. The shares fell about 10% the next day. Musk's SpaceX listed its shares in June in the biggest stock market debut ever, competing for the same investors.
why: -26%: the gap between the AI valuation and the car profits showed again; Tesla's value fell back below 1 trillion dollars.
source: Tesla Q2 2026 Production and Deliveries, 2 July 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026046717/exhibit99111111.htm (read 2026-10-03); Electrek, 'Tesla (TSLA) releases Q2 2026 financial results: record revenue, big profit miss', 22 July 2026, https://electrek.co/2026/07/22/tesla-tsla-q2-2026-financial-results/ (read 2026-10-03); 24/7 Wall St., 'Tesla Slides 10% on Earnings Miss Despite Record Deliveries', 23 July 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); NPR, 'SpaceX IPO makes history as largest ever', 12 June 2026 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03); https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/06/why-tesla-stock-plunged-26-in-july/ (read 2026-10-03)

title: Las Vegas robotaxis and the AI power trade lift Tesla
what: On 21 August Clark County, Nevada, allowed Tesla to run up to 5,000 driverless robotaxis in Las Vegas, the largest share of 8,000 permits granted to three companies. At the end of the month Musk said Tesla and SpaceX are each building solar panel factories as fast as possible to power AI data centres, and the shares rose again.
why: +18%, a partial recovery from July; the arc ends with Tesla valued as an AI, robotaxi and energy company more than as a car maker.
source: The Motley Fool, 'Why Is Tesla Stock Up Today?', 21 August 2026, https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/21/why-is-tesla-stock-up-today/ (read 2026-10-03); The Motley Fool, 'Why Tesla Stock Stepped on the Gas Monday Morning', 31 August 2026, https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/31/why-tesla-stock-stepped-on-the-gas-monday-morning/ (read 2026-10-03)
